answer: **Hypothesis (final candidate):** In the scenario of plots surrounded by contemporary urban land cover — i.e., plots embedded in landscapes with a high percentage of urban land use, measured as urban cover within a 500–1000 m buffer of the plot in the 2009 land-cover snapshot — urban land use was positively associated with the invasion of a **specific type** of non-native plant: species introduced **unintentionally (accidentally)** through global trade, tourism and contaminated seed (the *Unintentional* introduction pathway, as opposed to deliberate Gardening/ornamental or AgriForest/crop introductions). Controlling for elevation, climate (temperature, rainfall, solar radiation), surrounding cropland and distance to roads/streams, each +1 SD of 2009 urban cover at 500–1000 m was associated with ~26–31% higher counts of unintentionally introduced aliens (negative-binomial GLMs: coef +0.27–0.30, p=0.002–0.010); the effect was not explained by spatial position (it strengthened to coef +0.42, p<0.001 when coordinates were added), was positive in all nine year×buffer robustness cells (significant in six, strongest at the 2009 broad buffers), and the Unintentional share of invaders rose from ~56% (low-urban quartile) to ~70% (high-urban quartile). By contrast, urban cover did not significantly promote Gardening introductions (coef +0.08–0.15, p=0.15–0.49) and showed no-to-negative association with AgriForest introductions (coef −0.13 to −0.29, n.s.). **This is an observational association, not a causal demonstration** — it indicates that urbanized landscape settings co-occur with, and are a landscape-level correlate of, accidental-type non-native plant invasion in the Barcelona province.

payload.hypothesis: In the scenario of plots surrounded by contemporary urban land cover — urban cover percentage within a 500–1000 m buffer in the 2009 snapshot — higher urban land use was positively associated (observationally, not causally) with the invasion of non-native plants introduced unintentionally/accidentally (Unintentional pathway), robust to elevation, climate, cropland and road/stream distance (negative-binomial GLMs, coef +0.27–0.30 per +1 SD, p<0.01), to spatial position, and across 1956/1993/2009 × 50/500/1000 m robustness cells; urban cover did not promote Gardening (weak, n.s.) or AgriForest (no-to-negative) introductions, and raised the Unintentional share of invaders from ~56% to ~70% between low- and high-urban quartiles.
payload.workflow: Loaded all four datasets (12-row pathway×period trend table; 100-tip Newick tree overlapping 81/81 species; 81-species trait file with 2 dropped all-NA 'relative' columns; 632-plot niche/land-use file with 0 NAs, 10 habitats, urban/cropland at 3 years × 3 buffers, and 50-m progressive/regressive/no-change windows). Primary analysis: per-pathway negative-binomial (NB2 with estimated alpha) GLMs of n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo/n.total on standardized urban cover with a fixed covariate set {elevation, cropland.2009.1000m, annual temperature/rainfall/radiation, distance-to-road, distance-to-stream}; pre-specified primary cell = 2009 × (500 m, 1000 m). Robustness: (i) 3×3 year×buffer grid for all four responses; (ii) spatial controls (lon/lat, linear and quadratic); (iii) habitat: full urban×habitat interaction on total richness (non-significant) and per-habitat subset models (largely non-convergent → reported as limitation; habitat excluded from the primary model because it is collinear with urban cover); (iv) composition: Poisson offset models with exposure=total richness on invaded plots plus observed share quartile comparisons. Supporting: species-level trait means by pathway with Kruskal–Wallis tests (PGLS not run — R/phylo packages unavailable; caveat noted), and the temporal introduction-trend table as context. All numeric outputs written to results/.
